CG_CLOUD_ACCOUNT_ID.description: Optional CloudGuard cloud account id to scope the listing. Forwarded to GET /v1/findings as the cloudAccountId query parameter so the tenant only paginates findings for that account; when blank the importer queries every cloud account the service account can see.

CG_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Forwarded to CloudGuard as the severity query parameter (so the tenant only paginates results that survive the floor) AND enforced client-side after Faraday severity normalisation (handles CloudGuard's Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational enum and CVSS / score base-score fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: checkpoint_cloudguard
title: Check Point CloudGuard (CNAPP)
description: Check Point CloudGuard Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP / CSPM) REST importer. Pulls cloud-security findings from a CloudGuard tenant via the canonical GET /v1/findings endpoint and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. /v1/findings is paginated via pageNumber + pageSize with cloudAccountId + severity query params. /v1/cloud-accounts is optionally consulted (by id) to surface account name / vendor / region metadata when the finding payload is compact (tolerant to 404 / missing). Each CloudGuard cloud account becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because CSPM findings live on cloud accounts / resources, not on IPs) with hostnames = {accountName}@{cloudAccountId}; per-account findings attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per finding id with [CNAPP] engine prefix, '{ruleName} on {entityType} {entityName} [{region}]' in the title, finding description / rule_id / rule_description / entity_type / entity_id / cloud_vendor / cloud_account_id / cloud_account_name / region / organizational_unit / status / severity / created / updated / first_seen / acknowledged / remediation_time / tags / score / vector in the description; remediation / remediationSteps / recommendation / resolution / solution / fix surfaces as Faraday resolution. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped across finding + rule + cloud_account), CloudGuard-Rule: pivot label, Compliance: {framework} {section} pivots harvested from complianceTags, CloudGuard-Entity: entity-external-id pivot, magellanUrl / consoleUrl / url and references / links / external_references URL shapes from both the finding and the resolved cloud_account. CVE list harvested from id / ruleId / name / title / description / summary (CVE-shaped token fallback) + cve / cveId / cve_id / cves / aliases (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes) + rule.name / description (deduped case-insensitively). Severity normalised from CloudGuard's string enum (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Informational — also accepts Important / Major / Moderate / Minor / Information / None / Unspecified / Trivial / Negligible / Unknown) with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric score / riskScore is given (≤0/>10 → info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); CG_MIN_SEVERITY both forwarded to CloudGuard as the severity query parameter AND enforced client-side after normalisation. Status mapped from finding.status (Open / New / Active / Reopened / InProgress → open, Closed / Fixed / Resolved / Remediated / RemediatedExternally / Patched → closed, Ignored / Suppressed / Muted / Dismissed / WontFix / RiskAccepted / Accepted / Excluded / FalsePositive / Expired → risk-accepted). Auth: CloudGuard uses HTTP Basic with an API key / secret pair tied to a service account (Authorization: Basic base64(<CG_API_KEY>:<CG_API_SECRET>) on every call); a pre-built Bearer <token> value in CG_API_KEY short-circuits the scheme so federated / JWT-style credentials still work.
